Transit Timing Variations: 23 planets, 70% agree to <1%
Eclipse Timing Variations: 14 planets, 0% agree to <1%

svg.text: If a and P were both measured and M★ were right, these would be narrow bells around 0. Instead each method has a spike exactly at 0 (a was computed with Kepler's law) and a
spread of ±0.05–0.1 dex: the planet's a and the archive's M★ come from different papers with different stellar models. Imaging and microlensing measure a without the law
(projected separation, Einstein radius), so they scatter most. A 0.1 dex spread is a 26% difference in mass.
